About 1,091 points came off the Dow in a single day — and if you hold a 401(k), an RRSP or any index fund, that slide is partly yours.

The Dow fell roughly 2% Thursday, Nov. 19, closing below 50,000; the S&P 500 dropped nearly 2% and the Nasdaq slid 2.2% — Wall Street's longest losing streak since 2024 (AP, 24/7 Wall St.). The trigger: fears the AI boom is overbuilt, talk the Fed may hold rates higher for longer, and Anthropic's record first-day IPO value near $1.76 trillion stoking valuation jitters (CNN).

The S&P 500 is the benchmark inside most target-date and index funds, so this lands on retirement balances in the US and Canada alike — Canadian funds hold plenty of US tech too.

My take: the AI rally made index investors look like geniuses on the way up; the same concentration is what stings on the way down.

Did this week's slide change how you check your retirement account? 👇
